```{r}
# ============================================================
# Eye Tracking — Multi-Poster Multi-Participant Plot Generator
# Fixed for iMotions RExtAPI format with trailing-comma #DATA marker
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(jpeg)
library(png)
library(grid)
library(MASS)
library(gganimate)
library(gifski)

# ============================================================
# CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================
ROOT        <- "."
SIGNALS_DIR <- file.path(ROOT, "Renamed Signals")
POSTERS_DIR <- file.path(ROOT, "posters")
OUTPUT_DIR  <- file.path(ROOT, "output")

# Survey slide names to skip (won't be treated as posters)
SURVEY_KEYWORDS <- c("survey", "question", "questionnaire", "quiz")

# ============================================================
# HELPER: Read iMotions CSV
# Handles trailing commas on #DATA and #METADATA markers
# ============================================================
read_imotions_csv <- function(path) {
  lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)

  # Match #DATA even if followed by commas e.g. "#DATA,,,,,"
  data_line <- which(grepl("^#DATA", trimws(lines)))

  if (length(data_line) == 0) {
    warning("No #DATA marker found in: ", path)
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Line immediately after #DATA is the column header row
  header_line <- data_line[1] + 1
  data_start  <- data_line[1] + 2

  if (data_start > length(lines)) {
    warning("No data rows after #DATA in: ", path)
    return(NULL)
  }

  content <- paste(lines[header_line:length(lines)], collapse = "\n")
  df <- read_csv(I(content), show_col_types = FALSE, na = c("", "NA", "-"))
  df
}

# ============================================================
# HELPER: Load poster image + grob
# ============================================================
load_poster <- function(poster_path) {
  ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(poster_path))
  img <- if (ext %in% c("jpg", "jpeg")) readJPEG(poster_path) else readPNG(poster_path)
  list(
    grob = rasterGrob(img, width = unit(1,"npc"), height = unit(1,"npc"), interpolate = TRUE),
    w    = dim(img)[2],
    h    = dim(img)[1]
  )
}

# ============================================================
# HELPER: Load + filter participant data for one poster
# Actual column names from iMotions RExtAPI:
#   Timestamp, Gaze X, Gaze Y, Fixation X, Fixation Y,
#   Fixation Duration, Fixation Index by Stimulus
# ============================================================
load_participant_data <- function(participant_dir, poster_name) {
  et_file    <- list.files(participant_dir, pattern = "ET_RExtAPI.*\\.csv$",
                           full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
  slide_file <- list.files(participant_dir, pattern = "Native_SlideEvents.*\\.csv$",
                           full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)

  if (length(et_file) == 0) {
    warning("No ET_RExtAPI CSV in: ", participant_dir)
    return(NULL)
  }

  et <- read_imotions_csv(et_file[1])
  if (is.null(et) || nrow(et) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Rename to short code-friendly names using ACTUAL iMotions column names
  et <- et %>%
    rename(
      timestamp = Timestamp,
      gaze_x    = `Gaze X`,
      gaze_y    = `Gaze Y`,
      fix_x     = `Fixation X`,
      fix_y     = `Fixation Y`,
      fix_dur   = `Fixation Duration`,
      fix_idx   = `Fixation Index by Stimulus`
    )

  # ── Filter to this poster's time window using SlideEvents ──
  if (length(slide_file) > 0) {
    slides <- read_imotions_csv(slide_file[1])

    if (!is.null(slides) && "SourceStimuliName" %in% names(slides)) {
      # Flexible name matching: strip punctuation/spaces/case for comparison
      clean <- function(x) str_replace_all(tolower(x), "[^a-z0-9]", "")
      target <- clean(poster_name)

      poster_rows <- slides %>%
        filter(clean(SourceStimuliName) == target)

      if (nrow(poster_rows) > 0) {
        start_row <- poster_rows %>%
          filter(SlideEvent == "StartMedia") %>%
          slice(1)
        end_row <- poster_rows %>%
          filter(SlideEvent == "EndMedia") %>%
          slice(1)

        if (nrow(start_row) > 0 && nrow(end_row) > 0) {
          t_start <- start_row$Timestamp[1]
          t_end   <- end_row$Timestamp[1]
          et <- et %>% filter(timestamp >= t_start & timestamp <= t_end)
        }
      } else {
        warning("Poster '", poster_name, "' not found in SlideEvents for: ", participant_dir)
        return(NULL)
      }
    }
  }

  # Keep only rows with valid gaze coordinates
  et <- et %>%
    filter(!is.na(gaze_x), !is.na(gaze_y), gaze_x > 0, gaze_y > 0)

  if (nrow(et) < 10) {
    warning("Too few valid gaze rows (<10) for poster '", poster_name,
            "' in: ", participant_dir)
    return(NULL)
  }

  et
}

# ============================================================
# PLOT 1 — Raw Gaze Path
# ============================================================
plot_gaze_path <- function(df, poster, out_path) {
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      x_norm = gaze_x / poster$w,
      y_norm = 1 - (gaze_y / poster$h)
    ) %>%
    filter(x_norm >= 0, x_norm <= 1, y_norm >= 0, y_norm <= 1)

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = x_norm, y = y_norm, colour = timestamp)) +
    annotation_custom(poster$grob, xmin=0, xmax=1, ymin=0, ymax=1) +
    geom_path(linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_point(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.4) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "Time (ms)",
                           labels = scales::comma) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1), expand=c(0,0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1), expand=c(0,0)) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = poster$h / poster$w) +
    labs(title    = "Eye Tracking \u2014 Raw Gaze Path",
         subtitle = "Colour = time progression (early \u2192 late)") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.background  = element_rect(fill="black", colour=NA),
          plot.title       = element_text(colour="white", hjust=0.5,
                                          size=14, face="bold"),
          plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour="grey70", hjust=0.5, size=9),
          legend.position  = "bottom",
          legend.title     = element_text(colour="white", size=9),
          legend.text      = element_text(colour="white", size=8),
          legend.key.width = unit(2,"cm"))

  ggsave(out_path, p, width=13, height=9, dpi=150, bg="black")
}

# ============================================================
# PLOT 2 — Heatmap
# ============================================================
plot_heatmap <- function(df, poster, out_path) {
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(x_norm = gaze_x / poster$w,
           y_norm = 1 - (gaze_y / poster$h)) %>%
    filter(x_norm >= 0, x_norm <= 1, y_norm >= 0, y_norm <= 1)

  kde    <- kde2d(df$x_norm, df$y_norm, n=200, lims=c(0,1,0,1))
  kde_df <- expand.grid(x=kde$x, y=kde$y) %>%
    mutate(density = as.vector(kde$z))

  p <- ggplot() +
    annotation_custom(poster$grob, xmin=0, xmax=1, ymin=0, ymax=1) +
    geom_raster(data=kde_df, aes(x=x, y=y, fill=density), alpha=0.65) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = c("transparent","#0000FF44","#00FFFF88",
                  "#00FF00CC","#FFFF00EE","#FF0000FF"),
      name = "Gaze Density") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1), expand=c(0,0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1), expand=c(0,0)) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = poster$h / poster$w) +
    labs(title    = "Eye Tracking \u2014 Gaze Density Heatmap",
         subtitle = "Warmer colours = more time spent looking") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.background  = element_rect(fill="black", colour=NA),
          plot.title       = element_text(colour="white", hjust=0.5,
                                          size=14, face="bold"),
          plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour="grey70", hjust=0.5, size=9),
          legend.position  = "bottom",
          legend.title     = element_text(colour="white", size=9),
          legend.text      = element_text(colour="white", size=8),
          legend.key.width = unit(2,"cm"))

  ggsave(out_path, p, width=13, height=9, dpi=150, bg="black")
}

# ============================================================
# PLOT 3 — Scanpath
# ============================================================
plot_scanpath <- function(df, poster, out_path) {
  if (!all(c("fix_x","fix_y","fix_dur","fix_idx") %in% names(df))) {
    warning("Scanpath: missing fixation columns")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  fix_df <- df %>%
    select(fix_x, fix_y, fix_dur, fix_idx) %>%
    filter(!is.na(fix_x), !is.na(fix_y), !is.na(fix_idx)) %>%
    distinct(fix_idx, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    arrange(fix_idx) %>%
    mutate(x_norm = fix_x / poster$w,
           y_norm = 1 - (fix_y / poster$h)) %>%
    filter(x_norm >= 0, x_norm <= 1, y_norm >= 0, y_norm <= 1)

  if (nrow(fix_df) == 0) {
    warning("Scanpath: no valid fixation rows after filtering")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  p <- ggplot(fix_df, aes(x=x_norm, y=y_norm)) +
    annotation_custom(poster$grob, xmin=0, xmax=1, ymin=0, ymax=1) +
    geom_path(colour="white", linewidth=0.4, alpha=0.7) +
    geom_point(aes(size=fix_dur), colour="#56B4E9", alpha=0.75, shape=16) +
    geom_text(aes(label=fix_idx), colour="white", size=2.2, fontface="bold") +
    scale_size_continuous(name="Fixation Duration (ms)", range=c(4,14),
                          breaks=c(100,150,200,250)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1), expand=c(0,0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1), expand=c(0,0)) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = poster$h / poster$w) +
    labs(title    = "Eye Tracking \u2014 Scanpath",
         subtitle = "Circles = fixation duration | Lines = saccades | Numbers = order") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.background  = element_rect(fill="black", colour=NA),
          plot.title       = element_text(colour="white", hjust=0.5,
                                          size=14, face="bold"),
          plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour="grey70", hjust=0.5, size=9),
          legend.position  = "bottom",
          legend.title     = element_text(colour="white", size=9),
          legend.text      = element_text(colour="white", size=8))

  ggsave(out_path, p, width=13, height=9, dpi=150, bg="black")
}

# ============================================================
# PLOT 4 — Animation GIF
# ============================================================
plot_animation <- function(df, poster, out_path) {
  n_frames <- 80

  df_anim <- df %>%
    mutate(x_norm = gaze_x / poster$w,
           y_norm = 1 - (gaze_y / poster$h),
           frame  = ntile(timestamp, n_frames)) %>%
    filter(x_norm >= 0, x_norm <= 1, y_norm >= 0, y_norm <= 1)

  cumul <- map_dfr(seq_len(n_frames), function(f)
    df_anim %>% filter(frame <= f) %>% mutate(anim_frame = f))

  current <- df_anim %>% rename(anim_frame = frame)

  p <- ggplot() +
    annotation_custom(poster$grob, xmin=0, xmax=1, ymin=0, ymax=1) +
    geom_path(data=cumul, aes(x=x_norm, y=y_norm,
                               colour=anim_frame, group=1),
              linewidth=0.7, alpha=0.8) +
    geom_point(data=current, aes(x=x_norm, y=y_norm),
               colour="white", size=3, alpha=0.9) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(option="plasma", guide="none") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1), expand=c(0,0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1), expand=c(0,0)) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = poster$h / poster$w) +
    labs(title = "Eye Tracking \u2014 Gaze Animation") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill="black", colour=NA),
          plot.title      = element_text(colour="white", hjust=0.5,
                                         size=14, face="bold")) +
    transition_time(anim_frame) +
    ease_aes("linear")

  anim <- animate(p, nframes=n_frames, fps=12, width=1300, height=900,
                  renderer=gifski_renderer(), bg="black")
  anim_save(out_path, anim)
}

# ============================================================
# MAIN
# ============================================================
run_all <- function() {
  poster_files <- list.files(POSTERS_DIR,
                             pattern = "\\.(jpg|jpeg|png|JPG|JPEG|PNG)$",
                             full.names = TRUE)
  poster_names <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(poster_files))
  part_dirs    <- list.dirs(SIGNALS_DIR, recursive = FALSE)
  part_ids     <- basename(part_dirs)

  message("Posters found : ", length(poster_files))
  message("Participants  : ", length(part_dirs))

  for (pi in seq_along(poster_files)) {
    poster      <- load_poster(poster_files[pi])
    poster_name <- poster_names[pi]

    # Skip anything that looks like a survey slide
    if (any(str_detect(tolower(poster_name), SURVEY_KEYWORDS))) {
      message("Skipping survey slide: ", poster_name)
      next
    }

    message("\n=== ", poster_name, " ===")

    for (di in seq_along(part_dirs)) {
      part_id <- part_ids[di]
      message("  ", part_id, " ... ", appendLF = FALSE)

      out_dir <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR,
                           paste0("poster_",
                                  str_replace_all(poster_name, " ", "")),
                           part_id)
      dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

      df <- tryCatch(
        load_participant_data(part_dirs[di], poster_name),
        error = function(e) { message("ERROR: ", e$message); NULL }
      )

      if (is.null(df)) { message("skipped (no data)"); next }
      message(nrow(df), " gaze rows | ",
              sum(!is.na(df$fix_x)), " fixation rows")

      tryCatch(plot_gaze_path(df, poster,
                              file.path(out_dir, "gaze_path_plot.png")),
               error = function(e) warning("gaze_path: ", e$message))

      tryCatch(plot_heatmap(df, poster,
                            file.path(out_dir, "heatmap_plot.png")),
               error = function(e) warning("heatmap: ", e$message))

      tryCatch(plot_scanpath(df, poster,
                             file.path(out_dir, "scanpath_plot.png")),
               error = function(e) warning("scanpath: ", e$message))

      tryCatch(plot_animation(df, poster,
                              file.path(out_dir, "gaze_animation.gif")),
               error = function(e) warning("animation: ", e$message))
    }
  }
  message("\nDone! Output in: ", OUTPUT_DIR)
}

run_all()
```
